classification.difficultyReason: Directly apply the taught Prim’s algorithm, selecting the cheapest eligible edge at each step; the supplied total provides a check.

content.prompt:
The weight of the minimum spanning tree for the graph is 31.
Draw the minimum spanning tree.

spec.description: Seven-vertex undirected weighted network. A is left, B upper-left, C lower-left, E upper-middle, D lower-middle, F upper-right and G lower-right. C–D–F form the rising diagonal. Ordinary source blue vertices and labels and grey edges use house black.
spec.mathematics: Vertices A,B,C,D,E,F,G; edges AB=5, AE=10, AC=11, BE=9, CE=6, CD=3, DF=2, EF=5, FG=7, CG=9.
spec.answerVisibility: All original edges, vertices and weights are permanent student-visible givens; no selected tree is shown.

answer.worked:
Using Prim’s algorithm, start at $A$ and add $AB$ (5), $BE$ (9), $EF$ (5), $FD$ (2), $DC$ (3), then $FG$ (7). Each edge joins a new vertex to the existing tree.

$$\begin{aligned}W&=5+9+5+2+3+7\\&=31\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Complete minimum spanning tree retaining the source vertex arrangement and showing only the six selected edges.
spec.mathematics: AB=5, BE=9, EF=5, FD=2, DC=3, FG=7; seven connected vertices, six edges, no cycle, total 31.
